what: The cited part matches the digest, and no later state of YK-369 is recorded at the Houthis' area or at place not stated (all its citations date 2025-06-22 to 2025-07-22). But the record's condition, 'Whether parties in the Houthis' area may deal with Kuraimi', is wider than its quotes, which put the bar on financial institutions, exchange firms and transfer networks: YE-B013 'أصدر البنك المركزي اليمني في صنعاء ، تعميمًا رسميًا ... قضى بإيقاف التعامل مع بنك الكريمي للتمويل الإسلامي'; YE-E367 'issued a circular demanding that all financial institutions immediately suspend transactions with Al-Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank'; YE-E1272 'تعميماً لمنشآت وشركات الصرافة وشبكات التحويل المالية المحلية'. One quote of the record says customers are not barred and the bank not stopped: YE-C367 'ولم يشر التعميم إلى إيقاف البنك أو إغلاقه أو إلى وقف التعامل مع البنك من قبل العملاء'; and Kuraimi says the circular is for exchange companies only (YE-C371 'موجَّه إلى شركات الصرافة فقط'). So Q1:134 ('parties in the Houthis' area are barred from dealing with Kuraimi'; 'forbids a connection to Kuraimi for sellers in the Houthis' area') and Q5:141 ('Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank's bar forbids an entry for it at the Houthis' area') read a bar on financial institutions as a bar on sellers and on the bank serving them, which YE-C367 contradicts; Q5:131 ('a provider can be barred in one area alone') and Q5:154 ('an authority can bar a provider in one area at once') say the provider is barred, where the sources bar financial institutions from dealing with it and say it was not ordered stopped or closed. Q5:154's 15 days to liquidate balances is the financial institutions' (YE-E368 'financial institutions must liquidate their balances with Al-Kuraimi Bank within 15 days').
fix: Record: condition 'Whether financial institutions, exchange companies and transfer networks in the Houthis' area may deal with Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank, under the Sana'a central bank's June 2025 circular'; state 'financial institutions to stop dealing with Kuraimi and liquidate balances within 15 days; customers not named (YE-C367)'. Q1:134: 'financial institutions in the Houthis' area are barred from dealing with Kuraimi ... The second fact bars financial institutions there from dealing with Kuraimi as of 2025-06-26; the circular did not bar customers (YE-C367)', dropping 'forbids a connection to Kuraimi for sellers'. Q5:141: 'the Sana'a central bank's bar on financial institutions dealing with Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank at the Houthis' area as of 2025-06-26' bears on an entry for it there; drop 'forbids an entry'. Q5:131 and Q5:154: 'an authority can bar financial institutions in one area from dealing with a provider', in place of 'bar a provider'.
read: The card only; YE-C367, YE-C371, YE-E367, YE-E368, YE-B013, YE-E1272 as the card quotes them; studies/yemen-cases/constants.tsv row YK-369 (no note).

what: Both cited parts match the digest. The IRG part holds against its quotes: YE-E950 (IGC, 2026-02) lists under 'Government CBY' (Aden) 'Resolution No. 547/CBY/2023: Regulated the provision of mobile money services by non-banking financial institutions', and YE-F129 'لايجوز لأي شخص في الجمهورية العمل كمقدم لخدمات الدفع ... بدون الحصول على ترخيص بذلك ساري المفعول صادر عن البنك المركزي'; the only other state at that place, 'banks only' [YE-E157, YE-E156], is of 2022-03, earlier; 'banks only @ place not stated' [YE-D091, YE-E156] describes the past ('وكانت خدمة الدفع الإلكتروني مقتصرةً فقط على البنوك باليمن'), not a later state across Yemen. Q1:135, Q1:141 and Q5:148 hold. Q8:178 says that at each fact's place e-money and e-payment services 'may be provided only by the institutions each fact names'. For the Houthis' area part (2026-02-11) the quotes are a description of two models in use, not a rule with 'only': YE-B072 'تعتمد المحافظ الرقمية في اليمن على نموذجين لبناء الثقة: النموذج البنكي المباشر' and YE-B074 'تبناها البنك المركزي اليمني بصنعاء من خلال تعاونه الكبير مع شركات التكنولوجيا المالية الرقمية ... وتمثل له مصدر للأموال الإلكترونية (E-money issuers)'. And the state 'banks and non-bank institutions' leaves out the permission the Houthis' area's earlier quotes put on non-banks: YE-E194 'expanded the scope of the type of financial service providers eligible to obtain a license to offer e-rial services', YE-E193 'to be granted permission to offer e-rial services'. Read with that state, 'allowed there only if Sharrwah is one' is met by any non-bank, so the point drops the licence at the Houthis' area.
fix: Q8:178: 'at the internationally recognized government's area, as of 2026-02, payment services need a licence from the central bank (banks and licensed non-bank institutions); at the Houthis' area, as of 2026-02-11, banks and fintech companies issue e-money in cooperation with the Sana'a central bank, and non-bank institutions there were made eligible to obtain a licence to offer e-rial services (2020)'; drop 'only' for the Houthis' area part, and say Sharrwah's offer would need that licence or permission at each place.

what: The cited part matches the digest, its quotes hold (the general sales tax law, 2001 as amended in 2005, on tax.gov.ye and yemen-nic.info), and no later state is recorded at the unified Republic's area. The location rule is conditional and is a requirement to be present in Yemen for inspection: YE-E1238 'في حالة استخدام المكلف لأنظمة الحاسب الآلي يعتد بالبيانات والملفات المستخدمة كبديل لتلك الدفاتر ، وفي هذه الحالة يجب أن تكون هذه الأنظمة والدفاتر موجودة في اليمن للإطلاع عليها من قبل المصلحة'. Q1:136 ('a sales-tax registered seller's books and computer systems are to be kept in Yemen') leaves out the condition 'في حالة استخدام المكلف لأنظمة الحاسب الآلي' and the purpose of inspection by the Authority. Q2:130 keeps the condition but says the fact 'forbids holding them outside Yemen': the source requires the systems and books to be in Yemen for the Authority to inspect, and says nothing barring a further copy held outside Yemen; no state bars it.
fix: Q1:136: 'a sales-tax registered seller that uses computer systems for its books must have those systems and books in Yemen for the Tax Authority to inspect, at the unified Republic's area as of 2005'. Q2:130: 'this requires those systems and books to be in Yemen for the Authority to inspect' in place of 'forbids holding them outside Yemen'.

what: Both cited parts match the digest and hold against their quotes: YE-E009 (OFAC, 2025-03-05) 'ANSARALLAH ... Yemen; Secondary sanctions risk: section 1(b) of Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886 [FTO] [SDGT]', YE-D852 (Treasury, 2025-09-11) 'subsequently designated the group as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) on March 5, 2025'; YE-A064 for the IRG part. The other states at the United States' area are earlier (revoked, 2021-02; SDGT not FTO, 2024-02), and none is at place not stated. Q1:143, Q2:125, Q3:150, Q6:91 and Q6:102 hold. Q3:161 says 'the fact forbids, at that place, dealing with Ansarallah'. The state is a designation, not a bar; the bar is in the source's text outside the quote, scoped to U.S. persons and transactions in the United States and with exceptions: 116-home.treasury.gov line 107 'Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC's regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.' For others the quote gives a risk, not a bar: 'Secondary sanctions risk'.
fix: Q3:161: 'the fact designates Ansarallah an FTO and SDGT at the United States' area as of 2025-03-05; Treasury's notice says OFAC's regulations generally prohibit transactions by U.S. persons or within the United States involving blocked persons' property, unless licensed or exempt, and others face secondary sanctions risk'.

what: Both cited parts match the digest; the Sana'a part holds (YE-A005 'conducting banking business without a licence from the Central Bank of Yemen, headquartered in Sana'a', 2024-05-31), and no state at either place or at place not stated is later than its part. But the Aden part's place, the internationally recognized government's area, is not the scope its source gives it. YE-D435 (World Bank, 2024-04-05, line 901) says without any area 'The Central Bank of Yemen in Aden regulates and supervises private banks and money exchangers', and the same document, same date, puts banks under both banks: YE-D423 'financial institutions with nationwide operations are subject to the authority of both', YE-D437 'The banking sector is currently supervised by both the CBY-Aden and CBY-Sanaa', and its context (lines 893-894) 'financial institutions that operate both in the IRG and DFA zones of control'. So Q2:122's 'banks being subject to the Sana'a central bank's licence and rules in one and the Aden central bank's in the other' rests on a place the source doesn't give; what the World Bank source shows is the Aden bank's supervision with no area, and both banks' authority over banks operating nationwide. The one state with the Aden bank alone at the IRG's area is CBY-Aden's own claim (YE-C049, 2020-02-26, 'الجهة الوحيدة المخولة ... هو المركز الرئيسي للبنك المركزي في العاصمة المؤقتة عدن'), earlier and not cited.
fix: Record: move YE-D435 and YE-D436 to place not stated (the source gives no area), beside 'Both central banks'' of the same source and date. Q2:122: 'banks being subject to the Sana'a central bank's licence at the Houthis' area as of 2024-05-31, while banks operating nationwide are subject to the authority of both central banks (World Bank, 2024-04-05)'; keep **Place** with areas under Yemen only as far as the Sana'a part bears it.

what: All four cited parts match the digest; the constant has one state, so no later state. The Cash Pay part holds: Cash Wallet's own page, YE-E762 'Cash Wallet provides the Cash Pay electronic payment service for e-commerce stores and applications' and YE-E763 'integrate the service step by step via API'. Two parts say more than their quotes. (1) Floosak: the only quotes are from Quality Connect's page on the Floosak wallet (qc-yemen.com, published 2020-05-27, modified 2025-02-16; Floosak's own domain was blocked, per the run's README), YE-C221 'بفضل الربط مع تطبيقات الموبايل، المنصات الحكومية، ونقاط الدفع، يمكن سداد الفواتير، سحب الحوالات، وتحويل الأموال بسهولة.' and YE-C222 '01. الدفع عبر تطبيقات الموبايل'. The page names integration for 'العملاء والوكلاء والصرافين', payment at points of sale and 'دفع المشتريات التجارية'; it names no online store, no merchant taking online payments and no payment API. (2) E-Pay: the only quotes are from a Packagist package, 'al-saloul/kuraimibank-payment', by 'Mohammed Alsaloul', a community-written PHP client, not Kuraimi's documentation: YE-E081 'the KuraimiBank-Payment Gateway serves as a vital component in Kuraimi's E-Pay API solution, offering domestic e-commerce suppliers a powerful tool'. Kuraimi's own page supports the separate part 'Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank's service' (YE-D976 'سهّل لعملائك عملية الدفع من تطبيقك أو موقعك الإلكتروني الذي تبيع فيه منتجاتك من خلال ربطه معنا عن طريق استخدام APIs.'), which no point cites. So Q6:101 ('a merchant can take online payments through Floosak's payment API') and Q5:144 ('Yemeni wallets and banks take merchants' online payments through payment APIs', citing Floosak alone) rest on a page that doesn't say it; Q8:179 ('at E-Pay's service a merchant can take online payments through its payment API') gives a community client's description as E-Pay's service. Q2:124's 'Local services take merchants' online payments through their own interfaces' cites only Cash Pay; the plural is wider than the part cited.
fix: Record: drop Floosak's service from YK-131's places (or restate its part as 'bill payment, transfers and payment at points of sale through integrations with mobile apps, government platforms and points of payment', per Quality Connect's page); mark the E-Pay part's source as a community-written client (al-saloul/kuraimibank-payment on Packagist). Q6:101 and Q5:144: cite Cash Pay (Cash e-wallet)'s service or Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank's service, whose own pages say a store can take payments through an API, in place of Floosak. Q8:179: 'Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank's own page offers sellers payment from their app or website through APIs (2026-10-10); a community-written client names it Kuraimi's E-Pay API'. Q2:124: 'Cash Pay (Cash e-wallet) takes ...' or cite the other services' parts.
